3. Being aggrieved by the decision of the Taxes Appellate Tribunal, the petitioner took preparations to file reference applications under section 160(1) of the 1984 Ordinance. Since there is a requirement of making payment of 25% of the disputed amount under section 160(1)(b) of the 1984 Ordinance, the petitioner tiled a waiver application dated 29-7-2020 to the respondent Nos. 1 to 3 under the Proviso to section 160(1)(b) of the 1984 Ordinance stating, inter cilia, that the required payment was highly onerous for it, as the monies received by the petitioner had already been spent for charitable purposes in the form of social business and the petitioner at the then state was suffering from a severe disruptive effect on its activities. Pursuant thereto, the petitioner received a memo dated 20-9-2020 issued by respondent No. 1 under signature of respondent No. 4 permitting the petitioner to file reference applications under section 160(1) of the 1984 Ordinance, upon payment of Taka 4,15,52,444 and Taka 46,02,05,721 for the assessment years 2011-2012 and 2012-2013 respectively. Being aggrieved by the above, the petitioner filed a review application dated 4-10-2020 to the respondent No. 1 and, thereafter, made further representations dated 20-10-2020, which were never disposed of by the respondent No. 1. It is stated that the respondent No. 4, in the meanwhile, issued demand note dated 27-7-2020 under section 135 of the 1984 Ordinance even before expiry of 90 days limitation period for filing the reference application, against which the petitioner filed Writ Petition No. 4597 of 2020 and a Rule Nisi was issued with a stipulation that the same shall stand discharged on 31-10-2020 and the tax authorities may issue demand note only after 31-10-2020. Thereafter, on 2-11-2020 the respondent No. 5 issued a demand note for Taka 17,37,63,779 and Taka 197,70,91,219 for the assessment years 2011-2012 and 2012-2013 respectively. Under the circumstances, the petitioner filed Writ Petition No. 7243 of 2020 on 15-10-2020 impugning the order dated 20-9-2020, but this Court issued Rule on different terms _asking the tax authorities as to why they shall not be directed to dispose of the petitioner's representation dated 20-10-2020. Thereafter, the said Writ Petition No, 7243. of 2020 was non-prosecuted on 24-11-2020 as being infructuous as the representation dated 20-10-2020 was disposed of by the taxes authorities by an order dated 16-11-2020 which is impugned here in this Writ Petition. Hence, this Rule. 

 25. By placing the case of AK Kraipak and others vs Union of India (UOI) and others (AIR 1970 SC 150), Mr Mustafizur Rahman Khan submits that the Supreme Court of India held that the power exercised by selection board is an administrative power and test validity of selections. The Court further observed that the distinction between administrative power and quasi-judicial power is becoming increasingly blurred; that to determine the nature of a given power, one must consider the power itself, the individuals it is granted to, the legal framework, the consequences of its exercise, and the expected manner of its execution; that the concept of quasi-judicial power has evolved over time, with powers once deemed administrative now being viewed as quasi-judicial; that the purpose of natural justice rules is to ensure justice and prevent miscarriages of justice; that these rules supplement valid law and have evolved over time - no one should be a judge in his own case and no decision should be given without affording a reasonable hearing; that additional principles include holding quasi-judicial inquiries in good faith, without bias, and not arbitrarily; that while it was previously believed that natural justice applied only when an authority was required to act judicially, this limitation is now challenged; that the rules should not be inapplicable to administrative inquiries, as both aim for a just decision; that the distinction between administrative and quasi-judicial inquiries is not always clear, and unjust decisions in administrative inquiries can have significant consequences.
